g1.label: 1. I was sleeping deeply when my alarm ___ at seven.
g1.why: A short action that interrupts a longer one takes the past simple.

g2.label: 2. While I was getting dressed, I ___ that my battery was empty.
g2.why: Notice is a sudden, short action, so it takes the past simple.

g3.label: 3. Lots of students ___ for the bus.
g3.why: They were already waiting when I arrived: an action in progress takes the past continuous.

g4.label: 4. When the bus finally ___, it was full.
g4.why: A single main event in the story takes the past simple.

g5.label: 5. I ___ past the cafeteria when I saw my friend.
g5.why: The longer background action, interrupted by “saw”, takes the past continuous.

g6.label: 6. When I saw her, she ___ a coffee.
g6.why: She was in the middle of drinking when I saw her: past continuous.

g7.label: 7. When I ___ to the library, every desk was full.
g7.why: Arriving is a short, finished event: past simple.

g8.label: 8. While I ___ for a seat, my phone rang.
g8.why: After while, the longer action in progress takes the past continuous.

g1.label: 1. When she arrived, she ___ abroad before.
g1.why: “Before” her arrival points to the earlier past: had + past participle.

g2.label: 2. By the time it finished, she ___ most of the information.
g2.why: By the time + past simple shows the other action happened earlier: past perfect.

g3.label: 3. Two weeks later, she still ___ how to register.
g3.why: This is the situation at that point in the story, so it takes the past simple.

g4.label: 4. She went at five, but it ___ for the day.
g4.why: The office closed before she got there: past perfect with already.

g5.label: 5. The next morning she ___ for 45 minutes.
g5.why: The next main event in order takes the past simple.

g6.label: 6. The adviser told her that she ___ the deadline.
g6.why: She missed the deadline before the adviser told her: past perfect.

g7.label: 7. Luckily, the adviser ___ her to register late.
g7.why: The story moves forward again, so use the past simple.

g8.label: 8. … because the same thing ___ to her before she joined.
g8.why: It happened before she joined the team: past perfect.

g1.label: 1. What ___? (the case)
g1.why: Past simple questions use did + subject + base verb.

g2.label: 2. What ___ when the timekeeper gave the warning?
g2.why: A question about an action in progress: was/were + subject + -ing.

g3.label: 3. First we ___ Case D.
g3.why: The first main event in the story takes the past simple.

g4.label: 4. While we ___ our slide, the timekeeper said…
g4.why: After while, the longer action in progress takes the past continuous.

g5.label: 5. Luckily, our reporter ___ the start of the pitch.
g5.why: She practised before the warning came: past perfect with already.

g6.label: 6. During the pitch, another group ___ a difficult question.
g6.why: A single main event in the story takes the past simple.

g7.label: 7. … because we ___ about money at all.
g7.why: Not thinking about money came before the pitch: past perfect.

g8.label: 8. In the end, the class ___ for our idea.
g8.why: The final event of the story takes the past simple.
